claims.text: The proposed alloy is a high-entropy alloy containing at least five elements at no less than 5 at.% each.
The proposed starting material is a single-phase disordered solid solution.
The proposed alloy is outside the Nb-Ta- and Ti-based alloy families.
Local lattice distortions are a primary governor of superconducting critical temperature and performance in the proposed alloy.
The multi-element alloy's average electron density helps govern its superconducting behavior.
Changing annealing time, annealing temperature, or cooling rate can systematically change local lattice distortion and short-range order while nominal composition remains fixed.
Thermally induced changes in local distortion and short-range order alter electron-phonon coupling.
Local distortions and changes in electronic structure shift the phonon spectrum and the density of states near the Fermi level.
Changes in the phonon spectrum and Fermi-level density of states modify electron-phonon coupling strength.
Superconductivity in the proposed alloy is driven by conventional BCS electron-phonon pairing.
Increasing lattice distortion through selected annealing or faster cooling will enhance Tc by approximately 1-2 K relative to the homogenized baseline.
Increasing lattice distortion will raise the upper critical field relative to the homogenized baseline.
The predicted increases in Tc and upper critical field result from stronger electron-phonon pairing interactions.
The homogenized as-synthesized baseline has comparatively reduced local distortion and a lower Tc.
A primarily single-phase microstructure with minimal segregation is required for the proposed comparison.
Most high-entropy-alloy superconductors have superconducting transitions below approximately 10 K.
Partial ordering, spin-orbit coupling, or electron-correlation effects may dominate over the proposed lattice-distortion mechanism.
A lack of correlation between measured distortion or short-range order and Tc or critical fields would falsify the proposed primary mechanism.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome specifies a positive Tc shift of approximately 1-2 K, whereas the uncertainty field states that even the sign of the Tc shift remains uncertain.
